The device\n// matrices are padded up to a multiple of TILE; padding rows/columns hold INF\n// (with a zero diagonal) so they can never shorten any real path.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Fill the padded device matrices: everything is INF with a zero diagonal, and\n// the path matrix mirrors initializePathMatrix() for the padded entries.\n__global__ void padInitKernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                              unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                              const int n, const int paddedN) {\n    const int j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int i = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= paddedN || j >= paddedN) return;\n    if (i < n && j < n) return;  // real entries are copied in separately\n\n    dist[(size_t)i * paddedN + j] = (i == j) ? 0u : INF;\n    path[(size_t)i * paddedN + j] = (unsigned int)j;\n}\n\n// Phase 1: the diagonal tile (k, k) depends only on itself.\n__global__ void phase1Kernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                             unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                             const int paddedN, const int k) {\n    __shared__ unsigned int sd[TILE][TILE];\n    __shared__ unsigned int sp[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int base = k * TILE;\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n        const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n        const size_t g = (size_t)(base + y) * paddedN + (base + tx);\n        sd[y][tx] = dist[g];\n        sp[y][tx] = path[g];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    for (int u = 0; u < TILE; ++u) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n            const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n            const unsigned int nd = sd[y][u] + sd[u][tx];\n            if (nd < sd[y][tx]) {\n                sd[y][tx] = nd;\n                sp[y][tx] = (unsigned int)(base + u);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n        const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n        const size_t g = (size_t)(base + y) * paddedN + (base + tx);\n        dist[g] = sd[y][tx];\n        path[g] = sp[y][tx];\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 2: the tiles sharing the pivot block row / block column.\n// blockIdx.y == 0 -> row tiles (k, b);  blockIdx.y == 1 -> column tiles (b, k).\n__global__ void phase2Kernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                             unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                             const int paddedN, const int k) {\n    const int b = blockIdx.x;\n    if (b == k) return;  // that is the pivot tile, already done in phase 1\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int pv[TILE][TILE];  // pivot tile (k, k)\n    __shared__ unsigned int sd[TILE][TILE];  // tile being updated\n    __shared__ unsigned int sp[TILE][TILE];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int base = k * TILE;\n    const bool rowTile = (blockIdx.y == 0);\n    const int tileRow = rowTile ? k : b;\n    const int tileCol = rowTile ? b : k;\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n        const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n        pv[y][tx] = dist[(size_t)(base + y) * paddedN + (base + tx)];\n        const size_t g = (size_t)(tileRow * TILE + y) * paddedN + (tileCol * TILE + tx);\n        sd[y][tx] = dist[g];\n        sp[y][tx] = path[g];\n    }\n    __syncthreads();\n\n    // Row tiles read the pivot on the left, column tiles on the right; in both\n    // cases the tile itself is part of the dependency, so a barrier per step.\n    for (int u = 0; u < TILE; ++u) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n            const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n            const unsigned int nd = rowTile ? (pv[y][u] + sd[u][tx])\n                                            : (sd[y][u] + pv[u][tx]);\n            if (nd < sd[y][tx]) {\n                sd[y][tx] = nd;\n                sp[y][tx] = (unsigned int)(base + u);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n        const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n        const size_t g = (size_t)(tileRow * TILE + y) * paddedN + (tileCol * TILE + tx);\n        dist[g] = sd[y][tx];\n        path[g] = sp[y][tx];\n    }\n}\n\n// Phase 3: all remaining tiles; they depend only on already finished phase-2\n// tiles, so no barriers are needed inside the reduction loop.\n__global__ void phase3Kernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                             unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                             const int paddedN, const int k) {\n    const int bx = blockIdx.x;\n    const int by = blockIdx.y;\n    if (bx == k || by == k) return;\n\n    __shared__ unsigned int rowS[TILE][TILE]; The device\n// matrices are padded up to a multiple of TILE; padding rows/columns hold INF\n// (with a zero diagonal) so they can never shorten any real path.\n// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n// Fill the padded device matrices: everything is INF with a zero diagonal, and\n// the path matrix mirrors initializePathMatrix() for the padded entries.\n__global__ void padInitKernel(unsigned int* __restrict__ dist,\n                              unsigned int* __restrict__ path,\n                              const int n, const int paddedN) {\n    const int j = blockIdx.x * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    const int i = blockIdx.y * blockDim.y + threadIdx.y;\n    if (i >= paddedN || j >= paddedN) return;\n    if (i < n && j < n) return; in both\n    // cases the tile itself is part of the dependency, so a barrier per step.\n    for (int u = 0; u < TILE; ++u) {\n#pragma unroll\n        for (int r = 0; r < ROWS_PER_THREAD; ++r) {\n            const int y = ty + r * BLOCK_ROWS;\n            const unsigned int nd = rowTile ? (pv[y][u] + sd[u][tx])\n                                            : (sd[y][u] + pv[u][tx]);\n            if (nd < sd[y][tx]) {\n                sd[y][tx] = nd;\n                sp[y][tx] = (unsigned int)(base + u);\n            }\n        }\n        __syncthreads();\n    }\n\n#pragma unroll\n    for (int r = 0; Blocks are 32×8 threads, each thread owning 4 result cells in registers, with the pivot loop hoisted so the row-tile value is loaded once per pivot instead of once per cell.\n- **Predecessor packed into the distance.** Tracking `path` with a compare+two selects per operation made phase 3 ALU-bound (~300 ms at n=8192). Distances are held shifted left 5 bits on the device with the pivot offset in the low bits, so one `IMNMX` updates distance and predecessor together — and unsigned min picks the smallest pivot among ties, which is exactly the pivot the serial loop records. Kernel time dropped to ~195 ms. A device-side range check falls back to a plain (unpacked) phase-3 kernel if any input distance is ≥ 2²⁵; both paths are verified.\n- **Padding** to a multiple of the tile size with INF/zero-diagonal rows, so no bounds checks in the hot loop and any `-n` works.\n- **Transfer handling:** device buffers are memset up front (pays allocation mapping on the device side), and the initial `path` upload — which no kernel reads, only the final merge does — overlaps with the pivot loop on a non-blocking stream. Cells never improved carry a sentinel and get their original predecessor back in a merge kernel.\n\n**`floydwarshall/CMakeLists.txt`** — CUDA language enabled, `floydwarshall.cpp` compiled by nvcc, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`, same executable name, no new dependencies.\n\n## Correctness\n\nDistance-matrix hashes match the original serial code exactly for n = 1, 2, 3, 7, 17, 31, 32, 33, 63, 64, 65, 100, 129, 333, 512, 1000, 1023, 2000, 4096 — in both the packed and fallback kernel paths — and `-v` passes throughout.\n\nOne semantic note: the `path` matrix holds a valid predecessor for every pair, but for n > 32 it can differ from the serial code's when several pivots tie at the same shortest distance. That is inherent to blocking (it was already true before the packing trick), and `path` is neither printed nor validated by the benchmark.\n\n## Performance (RTX 3090, timed region incl. transfers)\n\n| n | serial CPU | CUDA | speedup |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1024 | 0.87 GOPS | ~256 GOPS | ~295× |\n| 2048 | 0.91 GOPS | ~480–740 GOPS | ~530–810× |\n| 4096 | 0.91 GOPS | ~590–875 GOPS | ~650–960× |\n| 8192 | — | ~1950 GOPS | ~2100× vs 0.91 GOPS |\n\nKernel-only throughput at n=8192 is ~2.8 TOPS; the remainder is PCIe transfer of the two matrices. Mid-size runs vary run-to-run because the first large pageable copy in a process is served at ~1.9 GB/s by the driver regardless of how it is issued — I measured pinning and explicit staging as alternatives and both came out slower overall, so the simpler pageable path stayed."}],"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":324,"cache_read_input_tokens":167999,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":324},"output_tokens":1,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"7ba28772-300b-4976-bd13-37c0241e76cd","uuid":"b2fd29b0-cd19-4fab-8cf6-6dd0a32c4c14","timestamp":"2026-09-05T17:38:51.695Z","request_id":"req_011CekhaA5qcTqi4nHeTjJ5M"}
